segments.text: Islamic contract law governs voluntary transactions while requiring lawful subject matter, genuine consent and compliance with Shariah principles.

Prepare formation of contract, capacity, offer/acceptance, subject matter, ownership/possession where relevant, and restrictions such as riba, excessive uncertainty (gharar) and gambling (maysir) in financial transactions.

Islamic contract law begins with consent and lawful exchange. Jurists analyse parties, subject matter, offer and acceptance, capacity and the legality and certainty of the transaction. The exact doctrinal vocabulary differs among schools, but the central concern is that obligations arise through a legally recognized transaction rather than through deception, coercion or an unlawful subject matter.
The maxim that contracts should be fulfilled does not mean every bargain is valid. The form and substance of the transaction must comply with the governing legal rules.

Riba refers to prohibited increase in transactions within the relevant legal categories and is central to the structure of Islamic finance. Gharar concerns legally significant uncertainty or ambiguity, especially where it creates serious informational imbalance or makes the subject matter, price or performance excessively uncertain. Maysir refers to gambling or games of chance involving prohibited gain.

Ordinary commercial risk is not automatically gharar. Business always involves uncertainty about future profit. The legal question is whether uncertainty is of the kind and degree prohibited by the law.

Sale, lease, partnership and agency provide the basic building blocks for many Islamic commercial arrangements. Murabaha is a disclosed-cost sale with an agreed profit; salam involves advance payment for specified future delivery; istisna is used for manufacture or construction; ijarah is lease; mudarabah separates capital contribution from entrepreneurial management; musharakah is partnership-based participation.

When explaining a modern product, trace the actual contracts used and the allocation of ownership, risk and payment. Do not assume that a different Arabic label alone changes the economic and legal substance.

items.text: Islamic contract law begins with valid consent and lawful subject matter, but the structure of the transaction also matters. The legal form should reflect the real exchange taking place.

Offer and acceptance create agreement; capacity concerns whether parties can legally transact; subject matter must be lawful and sufficiently identifiable; ownership or possession requirements may matter for particular contract forms.

Riba concerns prohibited increase in relevant financial dealings; gharar concerns excessive contractual uncertainty; maysir concerns gambling or games of chance. These concepts should be explained carefully rather than used as general labels for every risk.
Different commercial needs are served through different contracts such as sale, lease, agency and partnership. This is why Islamic finance cannot be understood through a single universal contract.

rows: Common confusion to avoid: Do not say that all uncertainty invalidates a contract. The concept is prohibited or excessive gharar, not ordinary commercial uncertainty in every transaction.

items.text: Learn contract essentials before studying named contracts.
Prepare the difference between sale, lease, partnership and agency structures at a basic level.
Use modern Islamic-finance examples only when their structure is correctly understood.

segments.text: Consent and lawful subject matter are basic.
Riba and prohibited uncertainty affect financial validity.
Islamic commercial law uses multiple contract forms rather than one universal financing contract.
